step7_1gib_scale_closure.scope: This is what actually closes Step 7. current_requalification (source_commit 7faf85f) above requalified only the harness itself against post-Faz-A production code, at dev-mode (64 MiB) scale; its own scope note says explicitly it does not qualify 1/10/25/50 GiB scale. This record adds real 1 GiB ordinary and 1 GiB TOAST-heavy Protocol B (existing-stream reanchor) runs -- genuine on-disk incompressible payloads, not sparse files or fake data -- against the current tree, plus three proven-and-fixed harness gaps found during this closure audit (see harness_corrections_this_round).

harness_corrections_this_round.change: missing_step_cannot_pass selftest gate previously only exercised the tracker generic step_one/step_two contract; POC_SELFTEST_FORCE_SKIP was read nowhere in the script. Replaced with a child mode that runs a real candidate build and real cluster bootstrap, never marks cluster_bootstrap complete, and asserts the real result.json is not PASS.
Protocol B recorded copy_window_commits (writer own counter) and commits_replayed (WAL-decoded count) as separate metrics but never asserted they match. Added the equality assertion.

Fixed a real bug introduced by the first fix: the new missing-step child block called bootstrap_cluster/install_oracle_sql from a point in the script earlier than their own function definitions (command not found). Moved the block after the shared function definitions so it genuinely exercises them (confirmed via ephemeral_disk_bytes changing from 0 to a real ~48 MB cluster footprint).

scale mode (the actual 1 GiB run path) never crash-tested a real 1 GiB CTAS -- crash/restart/retry only existed in dev mode against synthetic 500-row tables at 64 MiB total run size. Added run_scale_crash_and_retry: crashes a real size_mib CTAS while pg_stat_activity proves it genuinely active, asserts no partial artifact survives restart, retries cleanly, verifies row-count/fingerprint match, and proves the shared slot stays healthy for a fresh table afterward.

DDL-queue-policy and xmin/vacuum-horizon measurement (dev mode only) used fixed-size synthetic tables and an artificial pg_sleep to stand in for a held snapshot; the ADR itself flags this as not extrapolating to a real 1 GiB+ hold. Added run_scale_operational_characteristics: measures a real ALTER TABLE queuing behind a real full-size CTAS AccessShareLock, and xmin/dead-tuple accumulation during that real hold.
